proposed.sourceName: Mufti Muhammad ibn Adam al-Kawthari — Darul Iftaa, Leicester (in 'Alcohol: Its Kinds, Usage and Rulings', central-mosque.com)
proposed.paraphrase: Within the Hanafi school the relied-upon (mufta bihi) fatwa follows Imam Muhammad — that all alcohols are unlawful (haram) and impure (najis) even in small quantities — so the strict Hanafi reading avoids added ethanol carriers in food.

proposed.sourceName: Mufti Ismail Kotwal — Mathabah Institute (Darul Iftaa) — Ethanol Alcohol in Food and Drinks
proposed.paraphrase: A contemporary Hanafi fatwa holding that the relied-upon position permits consuming NON-khamr alcohol in a non-intoxicating amount (following Abu Hanifa and Abu Yusuf), while advising it is better to abstain when an alternative is available — representing the permissive side of the genuine intra-Hanafi split.
